Context from a materials paper:
- Metals in corrosive service lose material fastest when sliding wear and corrosion act together (tribocorrosion)
- Equal-spaced Al/X multilayer: ~3 nm per layer, ~6 nm bilayer, ~1.74 um total on Si
- DC magnetron sputtering of alternating X and Al layers onto (100) Si, X first
- Films are periodic nanolayers with a bilayer period of ~5-6 nm
- Ti beneath the Al surface raises the work function, making electron loss harder and lowering surface activity

Panels:
- F4c: caption: Fig. 4. Typical potentiodynamic polarization curves of ... n-type defect density of all NMMs

Question: The claim under review holds that Ti beneath the Al surface raises the work function, making electron loss harder and lowering surface activity. Does the comparison in Figure 4c across the Al/Ti, Al/Cu and Al/Mg samples support this claim?
